cards.text: Paul, the apostle, is in Athens, waiting for his partners Silas and Timothy to catch up. Friend, I spent YEARS waiting in the back of a junk drawer, so I respect a man who can wait. While Paul waits, he looks around and sees that the city is full of idols.

cards.question: How does it hit Paul to see Athens full of idols?

answers.text: He's deeply disturbed in his spirit
He's impressed by all the artwork
He's happy to just go sightseeing

cards.question: Bothered by all the idols in Athens, Paul keeps quiet until Silas and Timothy arrive.
Paul reasons in the synagogue with the Jews and God-fearing Gentiles. Where else in Athens does he talk with people every day?

cards.text: Then some Epicurean and Stoic philosophers start debating Paul, and some of them ask, “What is this babbler trying to say?” BABBLER, friend? That's what folks call me when I start explaining oven temperatures.

cards.question: Other philosophers say Paul seems to be advocating foreign gods. Why do they say that?

answers.text: He's proclaiming the good news of Jesus and the resurrection
He's carrying little idols from his own homeland
He's preaching to them in a language they don't know

cards.text: So the philosophers take Paul and bring him to the Areopagus, and friend, they are CURIOUS. It's a customer leaning over my counter going, 'Okay, okay, what's IN this one?'

cards.question: At the Areopagus, the philosophers order Paul to stop teaching about Jesus.
The philosophers want to know what Paul's strange new teaching means. How do the Athenians and the foreigners living in Athens spend their time?

answers.text: Hearing and talking about new ideas
Building new temples for their gods

cards.text: A whole city doing nothing but chasing the next new idea? That's a whole town hitting refresh ALL DAY. And Paul is about to give them something to talk about.

Paul stands up in the meeting of the Areopagus and says, “Men of Athens, I see that in every way you are very religious.” Friend, if you put me in front of a crowd like that, I freeze up and start listing toppings out loud.
Paul tells them that as he walked around looking at their objects of worship, he even found an altar with this inscription: TO AN UNKNOWN GOD. That's a birthday card addressed 'To Whoever.'

cards.question: What does Paul tell the Athenians about the God they worship as unknown at that altar?

answers.text: He's the God Paul now proclaims to them
He's too far away for anyone to know
He's just one god among their many

cards.text: Then Paul tells them who this God is. He's the God who made the world and everything in it, the Lord of heaven and earth.

cards.question: Paul says the God who made the world lives in temples made by human hands.
Paul says God isn't served by human hands as if He needed anything. Why not?

answers.text: He gives everyone life and breath and everything else
He would rather be left alone by the people He made
He only accepts service from His priests in Jerusalem

cards.text: Paul goes back to the very beginning: from one man, God made every nation of men to live on the whole earth.

cards.question: God made every nation from one man. What else does Paul say God determined for those nations?

answers.text: Their appointed times and the boundaries of their lands
Which of the gods each nation should bow down to
The names of every king who would rule over them

cards.question: Paul tells the Athenians what God intended for all those nations. What was it?

answers.text: That they would seek Him and find Him
That they would build Him great altars
That they would stay far away from Him

cards.question: Paul tells the Athenians that God is far from each one of us.

cards.text: Paul goes even further: “For in Him we live and move and have our being.” Not near Him, friend. IN Him.
Then Paul quotes some of their own poets back to them: “We are His offspring.” That's like winning an argument with a screenshot of the other guy's own text.

cards.question: Paul says that since we are God's offspring, we shouldn't think the Divine Being is like something. Like what?

answers.text: An image of gold or silver or stone
A great king seated on a throne
A light too bright for eyes to see

cards.text: Paul says God overlooked the ignorance of earlier times. But now, friend, the timer just went off.

cards.question: Paul says God now commands all people everywhere to ___.
Paul says God has set a day. What will God do on that day by the Man He has appointed?
Paul says God has given proof of this to everyone by ___ the Man He appointed from the ___.

cards.text: When they hear Paul talk about the resurrection of the dead, the reactions start rolling in. It's like scrolling the comments under a post, friend.

cards.question: When they hear Paul talk about the resurrection of the dead, what do some of them do?

answers.text: Drag him out to stone him

cards.question: Others at the Areopagus tell Paul they want to hear him again on the topic of the resurrection.

cards.text: At that, Paul leaves the Areopagus. One speech to a city full of new ideas, and he's out the door.

cards.question: Some people join Paul and believe. Who is one of them?

cards.text: A woman named Damaris believes too, along with others who were with them. Hang on to your apron, friend, because Paul's journey isn't over.
